title: A minimal model of money creation under regulatory constraints
abstract: arXiv:2410.18145v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We propose a minimal model of the secured interbank network able to shed light on recent money markets puzzles. We find that excess liquidity emerges due to the interactions between the reserves and liquidity ratio constraints; the appearance of evergreen repurchase agreements and collateral re-use emerges as a simple answer to banks' counterparty risk and liquidity ratio regulation. In line with prevailing theories, re-use increases with collateral scarcity. In our agent-based model, banks create money endogenously to meet the funding requests of economic agents. The latter generate payment shocks to the banking system by reallocating their deposits. Banks absorbs these shocks thanks to repurchase agreements, while respecting reserves, liquidity, and leverage constraints. translated_title: 监管约束下货币创造的最小模型

tldr: 该研究提出了一个担保型银行间网络的最小化模型，揭示了银行在准备金、流动性和杠杆监管约束下，通过回购协议和抵押品再使用内生地创造货币并吸收支付冲击，由此形成的网络比无担保网络更密集且更具抗压力韧性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a minimal model of the secured interbank network, revealing that banks endogenously create money through repurchase agreements and collateral re-use under reserve, liquidity, and leverage constraints, resulting in a denser and more stress-resilient network than unsecured ones.
